videos.caption: 9 Best Things to Do in Marrakesh 🕌✨ 1) Stay in a Riad 🛏️  feel the authentic Moroccan vibe, from the mosaic tiles to the whisper-quiet courtyards. Riads offer privacy, fewer crowds, and a home-away-from-home feel with traditional decor, often a peaceful rooftop terrace, and staff who treat you like family. Perfect for a truly Moroccan experience without the hotel hustle. 2) Best Coffee at Bacha Coffee ☕️✨ (Location: https://goo.gl/maps/6u3Xx9J9xqv1w9Qw7) Silky espresso, perfectly balanced blends, and a chic, relaxed atmosphere. Great latte art, friendly baristas, and a bright, stylish space to post your vibes. Pro tip: try their signature crush coffee and pastry pairing. 3) Explore the Souks 🧿🌀 Fun tip: haggle with a smile, never agree to the first price! Make it a playful game, sample spices, and test your bargaining skills. Lose yourself in ribbons of color, leather, pottery, and lamps. The thrill of the find is half the fun! 4) Visit Ben Youssef Madrasa 🕌 A jaw-dropping historic site with intricate tilework, carved wood, and serene courtyards. It’s a perfect spot for photos that scream old-world Marrakech charm. 5) Jardin Majorelle 🌿💙 iconic cobalt-blue paths, lush botanical displays, and a peaceful escape from the market buzz. A must-see for color lovers and plant enthusiasts, plus it’s connected to the Yves Saint Laurent legacy. 6) Ourika Valley Day Trip 🚙🌄 about 1 hour from central Marrakech (depending on traffic). What to expect: stunning valley scenery, Berber villages, waterfalls, and a cooler climate. A refreshing break from the medina with photo-worthy viewpoints. 7) Agafay Desert Experience 🐫🏜️ Highlights: camel ride under the open sky, squad  bike moments, and magical desert views. Luxe touch: stay at a desert camp with plush lounges, gourmet meals, and starlit dinners. Perfect for a memorable  outing. 8) Dinner at La Trattoria 🍝🇮🇹  warm, cozy ambiance with authentic Italian flavors in Marrakech. Great for a relaxed evening, fresh pastas, and a lively dining vibe after a day of exploration. 9) Jemaa el-Fnaa - The Heart of Marrakech 🎭💃 Do it for the vibes: bustling square, street performances, snake charmers, and a feast for the senses. Pro tip: bring some cash for photos with performers and for quick bites. Best times: late afternoon into evening when the energy peaks. #Marrakesh #Morocco #TravelTikTok #Riads #Souks

😍Morocco like Pinterest: the most beautiful hotels  🇲🇦  📍 Royal Mansour Marrakech One of the most luxurious hotels in the world, where every guest stays in a private riad with its own courtyard and pool. Carved ceilings, mosaics, and palm gardens. Breakfasts on the terrace and a spa under a glass dome. 📍 El Fenn A place where Morocco meets contemporary art. Bright walls, terracotta rooftop pools, vintage furniture, and rich colors. A bohemian vibe with sunsets overlooking the medina. 📍 La Mamounia A true Marrakech legend. Expansive gardens, arched galleries, emerald tiles, and a pool you’ll want to spend all day in. Classic luxury with history. 📍 Riad Yasmine The iconic Instagram riad with an emerald pool and pink walls. Small, cozy, and incredibly photogenic. Breakfast by the pool with flower petals. 📍 Amanjena Minimalism with Moroccan architecture. Sandy tones, reflective pools, and perfect symmetry. 📍 Kasbah Tamadot A hotel in the Atlas Mountains with views over the valleys. Terraces, Berber style, and warm sunset light. 📍 The Oberoi Marrakech Modern luxury with an oriental touch. Grand pools, arches, reflective water, and clean geometry. 📍 Scarabeo Camp White tents in the Agafay desert. Minimalism, sand dunes, camels, and caramel-colored sunsets. #moroccotravel #luxuryhotels #riadlife #travelinspo #bucketlist

It works at the airport, you set your own price, so there’s no negotiation needed 🚖  2️⃣ Be aware of the animal abuse at Jemaa el-Fnaa. Men walk the square with monkeys in chains and snakes with their teeth removed, don’t pay if they confront you 🙊  3️⃣ Where you stay matters. I found my riad on the @cozycozy app, which compared the prices across all the major booking sites. Agoda was £40 vs £45 on Booking.com, saving £35 over 7 nights 🏨  4️⃣ Eat all the street food. Vendors need licences, so it’s clean, fresh and cheap. I reccoemnd trying this sardine salad just off the main square, search “fried fish” on google maps 🍗  5️⃣ Stay safe in the medina. Before giving your opinion about Morocco, you should obviously do a little research first. Step one: open a book about Moroccan history. Yes, an actual book with pages, because apparently watching a few TikToks is not enough to become an expert on an entire country. Start by learning about the Amazigh people, whose presence in North Africa goes back thousands of years. Learn about the different Amazigh communities in Morocco, their historical regions, languages, cultures, and traditions. You can look into groups such as the Rifains in the Rif, the Chleuhs in the Souss and southern regions, Amazigh communities of the Middle Atlas, and many others throughout the country. Because, surprisingly, “Amazigh” does not describe one single identical population living in one exact place. Then study Moroccan history before the Arab and Islamic periods: ancient North African populations, Phoenician and Carthaginian influences, the Roman period, and the different dynasties and political changes that shaped Morocco over time. After that, learn about the spread of Arabic language and culture, as well as the migrations, exchanges, and mixing of populations that happened throughout North African history. Then comes everyone’s favorite part: genetics. This is where you should actually read scientific studies instead of looking at one DNA chart on TikTok and suddenly deciding that you have discovered the complete genetic history of an entire population. Moroccan populations have a complex genetic history, with a major ancient North African component alongside influences from different populations that moved through and interacted with North Africa throughout history. Results can also vary between regions and populations, so maybe don’t take one study about one specific group and use it as the universal answer for every Moroccan. You should also learn the difference between ancestry, culture, language, identity, and genetics, because they are not the same thing. Speaking Arabic does not automatically mean having exactly the same genetic ancestry as every other Arabic-speaking person, just as being Amazigh does not mean belonging to one genetically identical population. Human history is, unfortunately for anyone looking for an easy answer, a little more complicated than a “choose your ethnicity” quiz. Then research Amazigh languages in Morocco, their history and official status, as well as the cultural diversity between different Moroccan regions. Learn how Amazigh, Arab, Moroccan, regional, and family identities can sometimes overlap rather than simply cancel each other out. Finally, after studying all of that, you might actually be ready to talk about Morocco without reducing thousands of years of history to two sentences you found online. If you genuinely want to understand Moroccan origins, you have to look at history, archaeology, languages, migrations, culture, and genetics together. There you go. You can officially begin your studies on Morocco now. Good luck with the curriculum. It’s slightly more complicated than expected. #morocco#aespa#ningning#ⵣ🇲🇦 #aespa

Would you wander Marrakech alone?  One thing I was honestly nervous about before coming to Marrakech for the first time was safety, especially as a woman travelling alone. Social media can make the medina look super intimidating, chaotic, and overwhelming, but my experience has actually been really positive. Of course you need to stay aware like in any big city, but I’ve spent hours wandering the souks, getting lost in little alleyways, shopping, stopping for mint tea, and exploring on my own and I genuinely felt okay. One thing that helped SO much this time was not carrying all my luggage around with me 😅 dragging a huge backpack through crowded streets instantly makes you feel more stressed and overwhelmed. I used @bounce luggage storage so I could explore Marrakech freely for the day before my riad check-in, and it made such a difference. I could actually enjoy the medina instead of worrying about my bags the entire time. Bounce has thousands of locations worldwide and is a super reliable resource if you find yourself in a similar situation as me. Imagine ruas labirínticas, palácios ornamentados, mercados coloridos, jardins exuberantes e uma arquitetura que parece saída de outro tempo. Marrakech é uma explosão de cores, aromas, sabores e cultura no coração do Marrocos! ✨ 📍 O que conhecer em Marrakech: 🕌 Mesquita Koutoubia – um dos cartões-postais mais famosos da cidade. 🏰 Bahia Palace – um palácio magnífico com jardins e detalhes arquitetônicos impressionantes. 🌸 Jardin Majorelle – um jardim famoso pelo azul intenso e pela vegetação exuberante. 🛍️ Medina de Marrakech – um labirinto de ruas, lojas e mercados tradicionais. 🧡 Jemaa el-Fna – a praça mais famosa da cidade, cheia de movimento e cultura. 🏛️ Ben Youssef Madrasa – uma antiga escola islâmica com arquitetura deslumbrante. 🚪 Bab Agnaou – um dos portões históricos mais impressionantes da cidade. 🌴 El Badi Palace – as ruínas de um antigo palácio de proporções grandiosas. 🧖 Hammam tradicional – uma experiência cultural de banho e relaxamento marroquino. Marrakech é um destino que desperta todos os sentidos e mostra um lado completamente diferente do mundo.
